html:
Algeria is the largest country in Africa, stretching from the Mediterranean coast deep into the Sahara. The map shows it from 1900 to 2010: first as a French colony, then, from 1962, as an independent republic.

Before 1830 the coast was the Ottoman Regency of Algiers. France invaded in 1830 and met long resistance, led at first by Emir Abdelkader, who held out until 1847. In 1848 France declared northern Algeria part of France itself, not a colony. Around a million European settlers, later called pieds-noirs, came to own the best land, while Muslim Algerians had few rights. Conquest, famine and disease cut the native population sharply in the 1800s.

After the Second World War nationalism grew. In 1954 the National Liberation Front (FLN) began the Algerian War, one of the bloodiest wars of decolonisation, with torture and massacres on both sides. It brought down the French Fourth Republic and returned Charles de Gaulle to power. Algeria became independent in 1962, and almost all the settlers left.

The FLN ruled as a single party, living from oil and gas. When Islamists were about to win elections in 1991, the army cancelled them. The civil war that followed in the 1990s killed tens of thousands. Abdelaziz Bouteflika led the country from 1999 until mass protests forced him out in 2019.
sum: Algeria is the largest country in Africa, stretching from the Mediterranean coast deep into the Sahara. The map shows it from 1900 to 2010: first as a French colony, then, from 1962, as an independent republic.
